title: 28 U.S.C. § 1332 — diversity and CAFA
summary: Diversity jurisdiction permits specified civil actions between parties of different citizenship to be heard in federal court when the statutory conditions are met. The ordinary statute combines citizenship requirements with an amount in controversy.

sections.Role in the course: Diversity jurisdiction permits specified civil actions between parties of different citizenship to be heard in federal court when the statutory conditions are met. The ordinary statute combines citizenship requirements with an amount in controversy.
sections.What to examine:
Determine the citizenship of every relevant party at the legally relevant time. Apply complete diversity where required, identify the amount genuinely in dispute, and check exceptions and statutory restrictions. Treat corporations, unincorporated entities, natural persons, and foreign parties under their respective rules.

Under § 1332(a) the amount in controversy must exceed $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs, and diversity must be complete: no plaintiff may share a state of citizenship with any defendant (Strawbridge). A corporation is a citizen of its state of incorporation and of the state of its principal place of business (§ 1332(c)(1)). The Class Action Fairness Act, § 1332(d), gives original jurisdiction over class actions with at least 100 proposed class members, more than $5,000,000 in controversy in the aggregate, and minimal diversity (any class member diverse from any defendant), subject to the local-controversy and home-state exceptions.
